subject: Re: Order Form liability waterfall + Security Addendum linkage
body:
Message 1 - 2027-05-22 09:03 - From: Ryan Stevens <ryan.stevens@acme-corp.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai; procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: 
Subject: ACME redlines: liability allocation + SecAdd tie-ins

Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are ACME's redlines to the MSA + Order Form and a short note on the Security Addendum. Two points we want to surface before legal moves forward:

1) Liability waterfall: ACME is asking for a clearer ordering of which cap applies first for a security event. We proposed: (i) Order Form allocation for data breach; (ii) then general MSA cap.
2) Security Addendum linkage: we added a specific breach sub-limit tied to SOC 2/incident severity and evidence of non-compliance.

We flagged consequential damages carve-outs and asked for carve-outs for claim types ACME deems "regulatory fines" and third-party security claims.

Attached: ACME_Redlines_0518.pdf (redline PDF). Marta from procurement will handle timing if we can accept language.

Can your legal team confirm Redwood's position on ordering of caps and whether you can accept a limited breach sub-limit (e.g., 2x monthly recurring for dedicated customers)?

Thanks,
Ryan Stevens
Senior Counsel, ACME Corp

---

Message 2 - 2027-05-22 10:15 - From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Stevens <ryan.stevens@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-corp.com
Subject: Re: ACME redlines: liability allocation + SecAdd tie-ins

Ryan / Marta,

Appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Looping in Sales (Karthik) and Legal (Lauren) — they'll run a quick internal playbook check. High level thoughts:

- Redwood's starting policy: single global aggregate cap in MSA with carve-outs (IP, indemnity, wilful misconduct). For security incidents we typically accept a separate Order Form allocation for high-risk customers, but we need to avoid duplicative double recovery.
- A breach sub-limit tied to objective SOC 2 failure or material non-compliance is reasonable, but we prefer a formula tied to fees rather than a multiplier of monthly committed spend for predictability.
- Consequential damages: Redwood's standard excludes indirect/consequential as mutual. ACME's ask on regulatory fines is common; we need to confirm liability for fines where required by law and where Redwood's negligence caused the fine.

Action items: Lauren, can you draft two short options (A/B) we can send back to ACME:
  A) Order Form first (sub-limit for data events = 3x monthly commitment; MSA aggregate cap remains)
  B) MSA aggregate cap first with explicit carve-out allowing Order Form allocation to apply only when incident is caused solely by Redwood and not by Customer misconfiguration

I'll host a 30-min sync if you want to walk through. Marta, is Friday availability OK?

Thanks,
Soji (Soji informal)
Sooyoung "Soojin" Lee
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none on this message.

---

Message 3 - 2027-05-22 11:48 - From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai; soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; Ryan Stevens <ryan.stevens@acme-corp.com>; procurement@acme-corp.com
Subject: Re: ACME redlines: liability allocation + SecAdd tie-ins

Quick sales POV to feed into options:

- ACME is a dedicated customer with a 12-month committed Order Form. If we can offer a limited Order Form sub-cap (not full uncapped exposure) we improve likelihood of close without changing MSA economics for other customers.
- Proposed practical waterfall (compromise):
   1) For breaches where Redwood is the primary cause and SOC 2 controls demonstrably failed, Order Form sub-cap applies first (e.g., 6 months ARR or 3x monthly commit, whichever is lower).
   2) If the breach is the result of joint causes or vendor failure, MSA aggregate cap applies.
   3) Explicit offset for insurance recoveries and customer indemnities (avoid double recovery).

I prefer concrete numbers to keep negotiations quick — throwing a range complicates back-and-forth. If Legal wants to start with 3x monthly commit we can pitch that and hold flexibility during the exec approval.

Also propose: an optional clause that elevates incident severity to "level 1" only when SOC 2 non-compliance is confirmed by audit or Redwood's internal incident review within 30 days. That ties the sub-cap to an observable standard.

Karthik
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

---

Message 4 - 2027-05-22 13:07 - From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai; soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; Ryan Stevens <ryan.stevens@acme-corp.com>; procurement@acme-corp.com
Subject: Re: ACME redlines: liability allocation + SecAdd tie-ins

Folks — draft language attached (Security_Addendum_v3_marked.docx) and a redline to the Order Form (Redwood_Proposed_OrderForm_redlines.pdf). Key legal positions and suggested edits below:

1) Waterfall clarity: We will accept an Order Form-limited sub-cap that applies only where Redwood's breach of its obligations under the Security Addendum is the sole proximate cause of a Data Incident. Language: "Order Form Sub-Limit applies where Redwood is the sole proximate cause of the Data Security Incident and such incident constitutes a material failure under the Security Addendum."

2) Cap size: Recommend starting with a conservative, negotiable figure — 3x monthly committed fees or $250k, whichever is greater, for this customer size. Rationale: balance commercial risk and enterprise expectations.

3) Consequential damages and fines: Keep mutual consequential-damage exclusion. Add an exception for regulatory penalties only where Redwood is adjudicated (final determination) to have caused the applicable regulatory fine through gross negligence or willful misconduct. We can't accept open-ended regulatory exposure.

4) Offsets and insurance: Require credit for insurance recoveries and customer's own mitigation to prevent double recovery. Also add a survival clause for 12 months post-termination for breach-related claims.

5) Evidence and escalation: Add a 30-day incident review and dispute resolution step before invoking sub-limit application to confirm root cause. This gives both sides a structured process.

If these points sound good, I'll prepare two short paragraphs to insert into the Order Form and SecAdd and send to ACME with our redlines. Marcus — can you confirm any operational constraints on evidence collection (logs, KV cache retention) before we send?

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Security_Addendum_v3_marked.docx; Redwood_Proposed_OrderForm_redlines.pdf

Message 5 - 2027-05-22 15:42 - From: Ryan Stevens <ryan.stevens@acme-corp.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai; soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai; procurement@acme-corp.com
Subject: Re: ACME redlines: liability allocation + SecAdd tie-ins

Thanks for the quick turnaround and helpful options. ACME is generally comfortable with the proposed structure — grateful to see the "sole proximate cause" trigger and 30-day review baked in. A couple of asks before we greenlight legal: 

- Can Redwood commit to preserving incident logs for 90 days post-incident for forensic review (we can accept redacted or aggregated format if necessary)?
- On the cap size, ACME prefers a predictable formula: 3x monthly committed fees (we can supply the monthly committed figure). If Redwood needs a floor (e.g., $250k), please state it explicitly.

If you can confirm those two points, I'll push to procurement to accept the redline and circulate for signature. We expect procurement approval within 72 hours once language is finalized.

Ryan
Senior Counsel, ACME

Attachments referenced: ACME_Redlines_0518.pdf

---

Summary / Next steps (internal):
- Lauren to finalize short redline paragraphs for Order Form and Security Addendum reflecting: sole-proximate-cause trigger, 3x monthly commit (floor $250k) OR alternative floor to be discussed, mutual consequential exclusion with regulatory-fines carveout for adjudicated gross negligence, 30-day incident review process, offsets for insurance.
- Marcus to confirm log retention feasibility (90 days) and whether redacted logs suffice.
- Karthik to prepare commercial note on whether 3x monthly commit with $250k floor is acceptable to Revenue and Finance.
- Soojin to schedule a 30-min alignment call with ACME (Fri preferred) and attach final redlines + DocuSign link for signature once agreed.

Files to write back to ACME: Redwood_Proposed_OrderForm_redlines.pdf; Security_Addendum_v3_marked.docx

End of thread.
